solve.controls: Five manual picks on the 889 x 588 Commons copy, each good to about 5 px: the outward pickets' north-east corner at its foot and its top (3.7 m, the record's reconstructed picket height), the inward pickets' north-east corner foot, and the nearest bottom corner of each blockhouse (the north-east corner of the south-east one, the north-east corner of the north-west one). Focal length held at 1000 px with the principal point at the picture's centre; eye, heading and pitch fitted by least squares. RMS 8.4 px, worst 12.9 px.
solve.limits: The drawing is not metric. It follows a Chicago Daily Tribune sketch (1899) of Albert L. Van den Berghen's 1898 model, and its plan is not Whistler's 1808 draught: the same fit puts the flagstaff's foot near y 139 where the drawing draws it near y 245, and no focal length from 700 to 2500 px fits both the plan corners and the staff. So the camera frames the fort for a side-by-side and nothing more; it is never a historical viewpoint, and no position, size or height is moved to fit it.
solve.card_members: Every building and picket row the picture draws, by its key: blockhouses 4 and 5, the ranges 6 and 7 and the north and west ranges, the magazine 8, the flagstaff and both picket rows. Left out: the two small houses (the picture shows neither where Whistler puts them; a small pyramid-roofed building stands in the inner north-east angle instead) and the parade ground itself.
solve.lighting: Overcast neutral review: the pen drawing's shading is hatching, not a sun.
solve.scene: Meshes share the flat review grade; the river bank, terrain and covered way are not drawn by the reviewer.

anchor_transfer.rule: Same world eye, basis, image, intrinsics and all fourteen world member transforms. No source fit, geometry, survey datum, grade or date changed. Original outer-picket camera retained. New camera needs a fresh generated comparison and human review; no matching verdict is inherited.
